UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulations; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April, which amended Law 10/2010 and introduced additional beneficial-ownership transparency obligations; Royal Decree 1/2020 of 14 January establishing the structure of the Ministry of Justice and the Colegio de Registradores framework relevant to beneficial-ownership information; Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July; Commercial Registry Regulation, Royal Decree 1784/1996 of 19 July.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Companies Act and the registered office must correspond to the effective center of administration or principal establishment within the statutory rules. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registration, mail handling and limited administrative functions if the provider permits use of the address and the company maintains reliable access to records and official communications. For manufacture of in-vitro diagnostic medical devices, a purely virtual office is not commercially or regulatorily adequate. The company should maintain suitable premises, quality-management records, technical documentation, complaint and vigilance systems, responsible personnel, storage and production arrangements, and evidence of operational control. Applicable principal instruments include Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, Regulation (EU) 2017/745 where relevant, Spanish Royal Decree 192/2023 of 21 March on medical devices, and AEMPS requirements. The manufacturer may require AEMPS registration or notification, conformity assessment, CE marking, an EU declaration of conformity, a quality-management system, notified-body involvement for applicable IVD classes, post-market surveillance and vigilance procedures.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate and provincial Registro Mercantil of the registered office for final statutory registration; notarization by a Notary of the competent Colegio Notarial.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July (Consolidated Text of the Spanish Companies Act, Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 20-22, 23, 55-58 and 61-64; Law 18/2022 on Business Creation and Growth (Ley Crea y Crece) for single-document electronic incorporation; Commercial Code Article 119.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) filed electronically through the Documento Único Electrónico (DUE) portal.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 27 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The SL requires minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (approximately USD 3,250), fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; capital must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or, under Ley Crea y Crece, by a notarial payment certificate; no state escrow is required, but the capital cannot be withdrawn until the deed is registered.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate of conformity with CTE DB-SI and final inspection by the regional fire brigade; structural load verification for the cleanroom raised floor and heavy immunoassay analyzers; municipal legalization report proving compliance with urban planning, accessibility and public safety requirements; occupational risk prevention clearance under Law 31/1995, covering chemical, biological, ergonomic and physical risks, and laboratory biosafety evaluation under Royal Decree 448/2020, including ventilation, emergency evacuation, PPE and periodic occupational health surveillance.

Paid-in capital rule: The SL requires minimum paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (approximately USD 3,250), fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; capital must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or, under Ley Crea y Crece, by a notarial payment certificate; no state escrow is required, but the capital cannot be withdrawn until the deed is registered.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); e-office portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (Sede Electrónica), with electronic filing via form 036/037 and SII web services

E-government filing portal

A Spanish SL obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from the AEAT Delegación de Grandes Contribuyentes or the local Provincia de Hacienda: (1) obtain a negative name-certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed (escritura pública) before a notary; (3) obtain a provisional NIF (NIF provisional); (4) file the deed at the Registro Mercantil within two months; (5) apply for the definitive NIF on form 036 within one month of registration; (6) register for IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) and VAT on form 036/037. A non-resident owner without Spanish presence must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) in Spain where required by Article 45.3 Ley 58/2003 (e.g., for large-net-worth or specific non-established operations) and apply for an NIF for the foreign entity on form 036 before commencing any Spanish taxable activity.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS); general CIT rate 25%; branch of a non-Spanish EU entity is taxed at a 61.2% effective corporate rate under the branch-matching rule where applicable, except treaty override). Territorial scope: worldwide income of Spanish-resident SL, subject to participation exemption (ART. 21 LIS) and CFC rules (ART. 100-108 LIS); non-resident passive income may be covered by the Transparencia Fiscal Internacional regime. Tax-Exempt Zone status: not applicable, except reduced IS rates and ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) regime for Canary Islands operations. — A Spanish SL obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from the AEAT Delegación de Grandes Contribuyentes or the local Provincia de Hacienda: (1) obtain a negative name-certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed (escritura pública) before a notary; (3) obtain a provisional NIF (NIF provisional); (4) file the deed at the Registro Mercantil within two months; (5) apply for the definitive NIF on form 036 within one month of registration; (6) register for IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) and VAT on form 036/037. A non-resident owner without Spanish presence must appoint a tax representative (representante fiscal) in Spain where required by Article 45.3 Ley 58/2003 (e.g., for large-net-worth or specific non-established operations) and apply for an NIF for the foreign entity on form 036 before commencing any Spanish taxable activity.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS); general CIT rate 25%; branch of a non-Spanish EU entity is taxed at a 61.2% effective corporate rate under the branch-matching rule where applicable, except treaty override). Territorial scope: worldwide income of Spanish-resident SL, subject to participation exemption (ART. 21 LIS) and CFC rules (ART. 100-108 LIS); non-resident passive income may be covered by the Transparencia Fiscal Internacional regime. Tax-Exempt Zone status: not applicable, except reduced IS rates and ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) regime for Canary Islands operations.

Available election forms

Spain is a civil-law unitary system without US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) reduced IS rate elections for newly created SLs (25% on first 300,000 EUR for small entities (type 26)); (ii) the ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) international holding regime under ART. 21 LIS with tax treaty network, which may be elected for inbound portfolio dividends; (iii) the Spanish patent box regime (ART. 23 LIS) reduced rate election for qualifying intangible income from R&D-derived assets; (iv) the indirect attribution of VAT groupings (grupo de IVA / VAT group in Spain); (v) the special deemed- attribution for permanent establishments of non-residents (ART. 22.2 LIS) for importing foreign-law transparent entities into the Spanish PE — combined with EU anti-hybrid rules (Directive 2016/1164 and Ley 27/2014) that disallow BEPS hybrid mismatches at the level of a Spanish SL receiving interest/royalties from a hybrid-payor jurisdiction; (vi) optional IS installment elections (payment options under ART. 40.3 LIS).

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de minimis threshold for an established Spanish SL (registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply of goods/services in Spanish territory). For intra-community distance sales of goods and telecommunications/broadcasting/e-services (except for the OSS 'one-stop-shop' scheme), the EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 (VAT turnover) triggers Spanish VAT liability; non-established remote sellers must register through the OSS-IOSS scheme for imports of consignments not exceeding EUR 150, and otherwise via form 036/037 direct registration.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Under ART. 21 Ley 37/1992, exports of goods to third countries or destinations outside the EU customs territory are zero-rated (exempt with credit/0% IVA) provided the goods physically leave the EU within 3 months of dispatch (art. 21.1), under the exporter's customs export declaration (DUA/SAD). Condition: the Spanish SL must be the exporter (the holder/consignor of the customs declaration) and dispatch/transportation must be effected to a destination outside the Community territory (outside EU, or under the customs free-circuit regimes: customs warehouses, free zones, inward processing). The claim requires the simultaneous completion of the underlying commercial invoice with the export declaration and proof of physical departure in support; professional certificate by the customs office if lost (per Art. 21.2). Zero-rating likewise applies to (i) intra-EU supplies of goods intracomunitarias transferred to VAT-registered customers under the reverse-charge (Art. 21.3) and (ii) services under ART. 25 (transformation-OUTWARD processing and International sales commission for exported goods; a processing or disposed goods service abroad satisfies other interfaces and supportive proof requirements for offshore services provided that the recipient is established outside the EU and the service is not connected with Spanish real property).

  • Código de aduanas: Declaración de Exportación (DUA) / Single Administrative Document (SAD) with requirement for electronic export clearance via ICEX/DMS - Export declarations are filled through DUA in the electronic 'CEDA' (borrador) with the Expediente de Exportación DE (Surveillance) and confirmation of exit
  • Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de embarque / Declaración Marítima de Carga) or Air Waybill / CMR (for freight land) / SMGS waybill and packing list (lista de bultos), if dispatch inland
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (Justificante de transferencia bancaria de entrada de divisas - Confirmación de pago SWIFT/MT103, with bank credit advice referenced to the invoice); complementary Proof of Export certificate issued by the customs office / Agencia Tributaria (Certificado de Exportación, 'ECAA'), when queried
  • Commercial Pro-forma & Final Tax Invoice (Factura comercial con cláusula IVA exenta ART. 21); plus the corresponding customs export file (expediente de exportación) and official receipt for logistics and destination-entry customs stamps
  • Alternative documentary proof for the three-month rule: EUR.1 / EUR-MED certificate details (preferential origin) or certificate of shipment if customs verified
  • Export Intrastat filing (modelo N-I-D-28) and supporting freight/insurance invoices to evidence cross-border transit

Mandatory SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time/VAT book clearance for taxpayers in REDEME (large companies with turnover > EUR 6,010,121.04), for monthly self-assessment schemes, or those in the simplified/agricultural/reinsurance special regimes; SII requires the registering/logging of all customer/supplier invoices into the AEAT e-office through XML via HTTPS web-services/API within 4 business days (max 8 calendar days) of issue or receipt (invoice record). Aggregated periodical returns (modelo 303 monthly or quarterly and modelo 349/390) remain due. For B2G invoicing to Spanish public administrations, the Facturae XML standard and the General Entry Point (Punto General de Entrada de Facturas, FACe) are mandatory. Additionally, under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), electronic invoicing (Facturae format or interoperable European EN 16931 formats) becomes mandatory for all B2B invoices between firms with the phased roll-out: companies with turnover > EUR 8M must issue and invoice system from 2021, all other operators from 2024-2025 (regulatory deadlines extended); SII data entry remains the primary real-time fiscal clearance channel for IVA, while physical invoicing is governed by RD 1619/2012.

AEAT audit units and the Oficina Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF) scrutinize zero-rated exports under ART. 21 for documentary evidence of exit (prueba de salida). If the export is not substantiated, the invoice is recharacterized as a domestic supply subject to 21% IVA (plus IVA-ES→ other Member State identification under the reverse-charge), with the consequent liability for (i) IVA not charged (principal tax debt), (ii) late-payment interest (interés de demora, Ley 58/2003 ART. 26), (iii) a proportional penalty under ART. 184 Ley 58/2003 of 50% of the omitted tax (reduced grade: 50%; if total omission exceeds EUR 3,000 or a sustained pattern, elevated quotes of 75-100% apply; public attack for fraud (ANVSA ART. 46/2016) 150%); additionally (iv) penalties for false or non-existent export documentation under ART. 201 (sanción por dato falso, EUR 300-1,500 and per false data, or 100% where evasion exceeds EUR 120,000); (v) the clawback of previously refunded IVA/IMV for which the record was used as ground for export zero-rating (duplicative repayment, with rectification under ART. 120.3 GST); and (vi) criminal liability under ART. 306 Código Penal (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) where the defrauded IVA exceeds EUR 120,000 or the facilitative offense is corroborated, with prison terms of 1-5 years and fines, plus disqualification.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies full convertibility for the euro on both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittance by a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to non-resident shareholders. Dividend distributions to non-residents are subject to Spanish non-resident income tax withholding at 19% unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty; this is a tax obligation, not a foreign-exchange control. Banks may require documentary support for statistical reporting and AML source-of-funds verification, but there is no prior FX licensing or conversion mandate.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No statutory surrender of export proceeds applies in Spain. Exporters may retain euros or foreign currency in freely convertible bank accounts, whether in Spain or abroad. Export receipts must be reported for balance-of-payments statistics to the Bank of Spain when they exceed EUR 50,000 per transaction or aggregate thresholds, using the T-1/declaración de transacciones exteriores filing mechanism. Conversion of foreign-currency receipts to euros is voluntary and subject to normal commercial banking terms.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) within the Eurosystem, jointly with the European Central Bank; the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores (DGTE) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation is the competent administrative authority for foreign investment and balance-of-payments reporting under Royal Decree 1816/1991.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for offshore digital EMI providers. Under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and Spanish transposition, only EEA-authorised or passport-licensed EMIs may lawfully provide payment accounts in euros to Spanish residents. Offshore EMIs without an EEA authorisation cannot provide Spanish IBANs or operate as primary clearing accounts for local operational cash flow. For a medium-risk IVD manufacturer with cross-border trade, a full-authorised Spanish bank is strongly preferred; an EEA-passported EMI may be acceptable only as a supplemental collection gateway, not as the main treasury clearing rail.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with multi-jurisdiction holding companies or opaque ownership in low-tax jurisdictions.

Root cause: Non-resident corporate shareholder structure with multi-jurisdiction holding companies or opaque ownership in low-tax jurisdictions.

Defense evidence: Group organisational chart, certificate of incorporation and good standing of each direct and indirect shareholder, UBO register extract with percentage breakdown, audited financial statements of intermediate shareholders, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters, tax residence certificates, and a copy of the shareholders' agreement or capital injection resolution.
IVD manufacturing classified as enhanced-scrutiny due to cross-border distributors, high transaction velocity with Latin American counterparties, and complex export invoicing.

Root cause: IVD manufacturing classified as enhanced-scrutiny due to cross-border distributors, high transaction velocity with Latin American counterparties, and complex export invoicing.

Defense evidence: Spanish AEMPS medical device registration or CE marking certificate, ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certificates, manufacturing site inspection report, signed commercial distribution and supply contracts, proforma invoices and customs declarations, track-and-trace shipping evidence, and a detailed business plan demonstrating the commercial rationale for the treasury flows.
Payments received from or destined to jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk for money laundering or with sanctions exposure, or frequent use of third-party payment intermediaries.

Root cause: Payments received from or destined to jurisdictions perceived as higher-risk for money laundering or with sanctions exposure, or frequent use of third-party payment intermediaries.

Defense evidence: Written AML/CFT policies and procedures, transaction monitoring and sanctions screening logs covering SWIFT messages and SEPA files, customer and supplier due diligence questionnaires, periodic PEP and adverse-media screening reports, copies of export delivery documents, and a declared purpose for each significant transaction family.
Disproportionately large or early capital injection relative to the paid-in share capital stated in the notarial deed, or rapid repatriation as dividends.

Root cause: Disproportionately large or early capital injection relative to the paid-in share capital stated in the notarial deed, or rapid repatriation as dividends.

Defense evidence: Notarial deed of incorporation and restated articles, capital increase resolution registered at the Commercial Registry, bank confirmation of share capital payment, projected cash flow and funding plan, transfer pricing documentation, and a dividend distribution resolution with corporate tax payment proof.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound capital routes: non-resident shareholders remit euro-denominated funds via SWIFT MT103 or, where the remitter is in the SEPA zone, a SEPA CT with ISO 20022 pain.001. Payment must identify the Spanish SL as beneficiary with NIF code and clearly state 'Direct investment in Spanish subsidiary - capital account'. For statistical compliance with the Bank of Spain, the foreign-investment declaration must be filed under the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores framework using the 'Inversión exterior directa' classification, and the receiving bank must receive a certified copy of the capital increase deed and the Commercial Registry filing. The bank will perform source-of-funds verification for the full amount; if the capital is remitted in USD, it is converted to EUR at the bank's open market rate with no FX control restriction. Beneficiary bank must release escrowed funds only after the notarial deed and regulatory licence (Spanish AEMPS registration for IVD manufacturing) are presented.Outbound clearing rails: euro-denominated supplier and trade payments are cleared via SEPA/TARGET2 and SWIFT MT103 messages; for high-value or documentary export transactions to Latin America and non-EEA markets, the preferred rail is an irrevocable commercial letter of credit confirmed or advised through the Spanish bank's correspondent network, using SWIFT MT700 series for issuance, MT707 for amendments, and MT710/MT720 as applicable. Trade settlements for medical-device components require the presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, AEO certificate where available, and customs export declaration. Repatriation of export proceeds from non-EU buyers may be received via SWIFT MT103 into the same treasury account; amounts over EUR 50,000 must be captured in the periodic Bank of Spain balance-of-payments reporting file. For intra-group transactions, transfer pricing documentation must be maintained to satisfy anti-BEPS substance requirements and to support the clearing rails used.Deliverable EUR/USD outright forward contracts with an EU-authorised credit institution for trade-receivable conversionSpot-forward FX swaps and tom-next swaps to manage intra-month euro-liquidity from USD-denominated IVD distributor collectionsCross-currency interest rate swaps for USD/EUR treasury liabilities or long-term lease financingNon-deliverable forwards for emerging-market currencies (e.g. LATAM currencies) only where the underlying trade exposure meets hedge effectiveness tests and an offshore deliverable market is unavailable

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for offshore digital EMI providers. Under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and Spanish transposition, only EEA-authorised or passport-licensed EMIs may lawfully provide payment accounts in euros to Spanish residents. Offshore EMIs without an EEA authorisation cannot provide Spanish IBANs or operate as primary clearing accounts for local operational cash flow. For a medium-risk IVD manufacturer with cross-border trade, a full-authorised Spanish bank is strongly preferred; an EEA-passported EMI may be acceptable only as a supplemental collection gateway, not as the main treasury clearing rail.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% standard Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Eligible newly incorporated companies generally apply 15% during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions. Reduced rates may apply to qualifying micro-enterprises and small enterprises under transitional rules.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring a minimum 5% participation, a minimum one-year holding period or commitment, qualifying legal form and taxation, and anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within the 25 calendar days immediately following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the usual filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the last day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing calendar rules extend the deadline to the next business day.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; electronic direct-debit deadlines may be earlier under AEAT payment-calendar rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the usual deadline is the following November.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 216 is generally due within the first 20 calendar days of April, July, October, and January for the preceding quarter. Modelo 296 is generally due in January for the preceding calendar year, subject to the applicable AEAT calendar.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spain generally does not require full related-party documentation for transactions of the same type and valuation method with the same related party not exceeding EUR 250,000 in the tax period. Separate lower thresholds generally apply to certain real-estate transactions and transactions involving intangible assets. Local-file requirements apply subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation rules. A Spanish master file is generally required for entities belonging to a group, with an important exemption where the group is below the applicable EUR 45 million net turnover threshold. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. These thresholds do not eliminate the arm's-length requirement or the obligation to maintain evidence supporting material transactions.

Economic substance scope: Spain has no standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore-jurisdiction ESR frameworks. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, the anti-simulation doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest-limitation rules, principal-purpose analysis, and EU anti-abuse standards require genuine commercial substance. The SL should maintain Spanish decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or controlled facilities where commercially appropriate, manufacturing and quality systems, inventory and logistics control, risk assumption, technical competence, independent governance, and contemporaneous records. A conduit company receiving royalties, interest, management fees, or dividends without functions, assets, risks, and beneficial ownership is high risk.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent Corporate Income Tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid or improperly refunded tax, plus interest and collection costs. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud may apply, generally carrying imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized conduct, may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for restitution and fines, and subsidiary liability for unpaid tax where statutory control, participation, or negligent management conditions are met. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures may be ordered in criminal or enforcement proceedings; imprisonment follows only a final criminal conviction and applicable judicial process.
False transfer pricing, concealed related-party distributions, or non-arm's-length intercompany charges

Statutory sanction: AEAT may make a primary transfer-pricing adjustment, secondary adjustment, interest assessment, and administrative penalty. Material documentation failures may attract penalties calculated by omitted or incorrect data or, where tax is underpaid, proportional penalties generally within the tax-penalty ranges applicable to the conduct.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil damages, tax subsidiary liability, and criminal exposure where the arrangement forms part of intentional tax fraud. Corporate separateness is not an absolute defense against proven fraud, simulation, abuse, or personal participation.
Improper dividend, interest, or royalty withholding

Statutory sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and proportional tax penalties. Treaty relief may be denied and the recipient may be required to seek recovery through a refund procedure.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur subsidiary liability where failure to withhold resulted from deliberate or negligent management. Fraudulent withholding certificates or sham ownership structures may generate criminal tax exposure.
Shell company, sham residence, or beneficial-ownership abuse

Statutory sanction: Benefits may be denied under anti-abuse, simulation, principal-purpose, and beneficial-ownership principles. Tax, interest, penalties, withholding assessments, and transaction recharacterization may follow.

Director personal liability: Individuals who direct or knowingly facilitate the arrangement may incur civil, administrative, or criminal liability. Courts may disregard separate legal personality in cases of fraud, abuse of rights, or unlawful asset diversion; precautionary travel or asset restrictions may be imposed by judicial order.
Accounting and statutory-book manipulation

Statutory sanction: Tax reassessment, bookkeeping and tax penalties, loss of deductions, interest, and possible criminal accounting or tax-fraud proceedings may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for creditor and shareholder losses, tax debts under statutory conditions, insolvency-related liability, and criminal offenses involving falsification or fraudulent accounts.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing failures

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements can produce substantial fines, including amounts linked to the transaction, annual turnover, or statutory maximums, together with public or private reprimands, temporary suspension, and management disqualification. Exact exposure depends on classification and the regulated status of the obligated person.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and de facto managers may be individually sanctioned or prosecuted for knowing participation, gross negligence, obstruction, or laundering. Asset freezing, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply in criminal proceedings after judicial determination.
Customs, VAT, product-regulatory, and medical-device misclassification

Statutory sanction: Customs and VAT reassessments, import duties, interest, administrative fines, seizure, market withdrawal, suspension of activities, and product-regulatory sanctions may apply. Serious product-safety breaches may trigger criminal liability.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil product liability, regulatory disqualification, tax liability, and criminal exposure for intentional trafficking, falsification, or knowing distribution of unsafe or non-compliant devices.
Failure to maintain transfer-pricing, accounting, or tax records

Statutory sanction: Specific documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. The absence of documentation also increases the risk of direct tax adjustments and broader penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur administrative or subsidiary tax liability where recordkeeping failures are attributable to intentional or negligent management. Criminal liability requires additional elements such as fraud, concealment, or participation in an offense.
Illegal profit distribution and insolvency prejudice

Statutory sanction: Improper distributions may require restitution, interest, corporate-law sanctions, and insolvency clawback. Directors may be subject to insolvency qualification consequences, disqualification, loss of rights against the estate, and liability for the insolvency deficit in appropriate cases.

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal restitution, damages, disqualification from administration, and criminal liability for insolvency crimes or asset concealment. Judicial asset-preservation and travel measures may be available in insolvency or criminal proceedings.
